text: Assumption: The presence of ValueOrThrow() alongside Value() and operator* in Result serves as a migration bridge for systems that optionally still support C++ exceptions, even though the AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform primarily operates exception-free — is this correct?
text_en: Assumption: The presence of ValueOrThrow() alongside Value() and operator* in Result serves as a migration bridge for systems that optionally still support C++ exceptions, even though the AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform primarily operates exception-free — is this correct?
norm: the presence of valueorthrow alongside value and operator in result serves as a migration bridge for systems that optionally still support c exceptions even though the autosar adaptive platform primarily operates exception free
assumption: The presence of ValueOrThrow() alongside Value() and operator* in Result serves as a migration bridge for systems that optionally still support C++ exceptions, even though the AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform primarily operates exception-free.
rationale: Result::Value() is noexcept, whereas ValueOrThrow() is explicitly specified as noexcept(false) (SWS_CORE_00755, SWS_CORE_00766).
